answer: Resist sybils with duration-weighted staking: an identity's influence grows only with capital locked for a long, fixed term, not with wallet count. A lone vertex in the trust graph counts for little until its stake has sat through many epochs. Splitting funds across ten thousand identities earns no extra weight, because each share is small and short. Crossing the tundra of a full lock term is the price of standing: an attacker must freeze real capital for months per fake, paying opportunity cost on every sybil, while an honest agent locks once and lets time, light as a zephyr, do the work.
